full_judgment: 4. The petitioner contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegation of the plaint and also contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form and manner and that the opposite party No. 1 has no locus standi to institute the suit. That there is no cause of action to institute the suit. That the suit is barred by principles of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and that the suit is hit by the provisions of the Specific Relief Act. The petitioner further stated in her written statement that 2.61 acres of land appertaining to Khatian No. 927 of Mouza Joarsahara originally belonged to one Ekbar Ali and for necessity of money to meet family needs the said Ekbar Ali transferred 4½ decimals of land out of 2.61 acres in favour of the petitioner by a Registered Sale Deed No. 420 dated 31-1-81 and delivered possession in her favour. That thereafter the petitioner got the suit land mutated in her name from the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle. The petitioner has been legally and peacefully enjoying and possessing the suit land through tenants as well as by her family members for more than 12 years by erecting 8 semipucca rooms and taking electric, water and gas connection and by paying rents to the Government. That in the last survey attested Khatian No. 44975 has been correctly prepared in the name of the petitioner. That the averments regarding execution of Bainanama between the petitioner and the opposite party No. 1 is absolutely false, fraudulent, fabricated and without any basis. The petitioner for the first time came to know about the alleged Bainanama after receiving the legal notice addressed to her by the opposite party No. 1 and that in order to grab the suit land the opposite party No. 1 has fraudulently created the alleged Bainanama out of greed and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
